pull.title: fix(admin): a pause writes the pause, and nothing else
pull.body:
A pause click cost seconds, and none of that work had anything to do with pausing. It now costs the write and nothing else. Separately, one entry in the 6.34.0 quota classifier was a bare word and had to go.

## What a pause was actually doing

`_apply_admin_config_locked` called `ProviderRuntimeManager.replace()` without `background_refresh`, which defaults to `True`. Every admin write — a pause included — therefore rebuilt every provider client and scheduled a full `/models` sweep. A pause is read off `Settings` at plan time (`routing.py`, `_paused_for`) and never reaches `create_provider`, so none of that work can change what a pause does.

The sweep also blocked the event loop. `ProviderModelDiscovery._refresh_model_infos` resolved each provider inside a loop with no `await` in it: an SSL context and an HTTP client per provider, entirely synchronous, and the task did not reach a suspension point until the whole loop had run. So `_cancel_refresh`'s `task.cancel()` could not land until the sweep it was abandoning had finished, and click N+1 paid for click N — which is where the alternating fast/slow pattern in the user's `server.log` came from.

## Measured, on a scratch server

Scratch MCC on `PORT=8199`, bound to `127.0.0.1`, scratch `HOME`, the user's 14 `MODEL*` lines copied verbatim from `~/.fcc/.env` with **fake** keys throughout and the custom provider pointed at a black hole — no real network call is in any number here. Identical env for both runs. `:8082` was checked free of this work first and the live server was re-verified `HTTP 200` afterwards.

| click | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 PAUSE | 7132 ms | **710 ms** |
| 2 RESUME | 11729 ms | **638 ms** |
| 3 PAUSE | 7254 ms | **682 ms** |
| 4 RESUME | 13156 ms | **772 ms** |
| 5 PAUSE | 6961 ms | **753 ms** |
| 6 RESUME | 12995 ms | **668 ms** |
| 7 PAUSE | 7301 ms | **757 ms** |
| 8 RESUME | 6934 ms | **758 ms** |
| no-op pause | 6937 ms | **751 ms** |

`ProviderRateLimiter initialized` lines logged **per click**: **52 before, 0 after** — every click, including the no-op. Across the whole nine-click sequence the after-run's log gained **zero** `ProviderRateLimiter initialized` and **zero** `Provider model discovery` lines; its last such line is from startup.

The residual ~700 ms is `prepare_admin_update` validation, measured in-process against the same env at **628–643 ms**. That is the whole of what is left and it is out of scope here: it would speed up every admin save, not just pause, and it is a larger change to the admin write path.

## The changes

**`background_refresh` is computed from the update, at the call site.** The decision is a manifest fact, not a key list written at the caller: `ConfigFieldSpec` gains `affects_providers: bool = True`, the six `MODEL_*_PAUSED` fields declare `False` beside their own label and help text, and `update_affects_providers()` answers `True` for any key the manifest does not own. A key added tomorrow is slow-but-correct rather than fast-but-wrong. The generation swap itself is **kept** — it costs under a millisecond and it is what makes a pause visible to the very next plan.

**`await asyncio.sleep(0)` per provider in the discovery resolve loop**, so a sweep never holds the event loop for its whole length and a cancel can land inside it. This helps every config apply, not only a pause.

**Two UI defects.** A failed pause reported only into `#messageArea` at the top of the page; the pause control's own panel (`#routeStatus`) said nothing and the row snapped back with no explanation. It now announces `Could not pause <ref> on the <route> route -- nothing changed. <reason>` in that panel, with no Undo button (nothing happened, so there is nothing to undo) while keeping the `#messageArea` message. And Undo passed `button: null`, leaving the row's own toggle live during its POST; it now passes the originating button, so the same disable guard covers both writes.

Driven in Chrome against the scratch server, three screenshots in `screenshots-pause-fix/`, **zero console errors**: a successful pause, a forced-500 pause showing the failure sentence in `#routeStatus` with the row back to `Pause`/not-paused/re-enabled, and an Undo held open mid-POST with the row toggle `disabled: true` (re-enabled and re-paused after release).

Kept unchanged on purpose: the disable-during-flight guard, the in-place patch instead of a refetch, and the dirty-drag isolation were already correct.

**Pause semantics are untouched.** Pause stays per rail. The USAGE and in-app Guide now say so plainly — *pausing an entry on one route does not pause the same model on other routes* — rather than changing what the button means.

## `QUOTA_PHRASES` no longer contains the bare word `billing`

The condition on the 6.34.0 classifier was no false positives, and one bare word cannot meet it: `billing` matches *"see our billing documentation for limits"* in an ordinary 400, which would classify a merely malformed request as `quota` and bench the whole key pool. It is removed and **not** replaced: no measured provider body was on hand to justify a narrower `billing ...` phrase, and the rule this list already states is that an entry needs one. The comment block now records why it must not come back. README and USAGE phrase lists updated.

## Tests

New `tests/runtime/test_pause_does_not_rebuild_providers.py` (5), with a fake resolver that sleeps 200 ms per provider so the wall clock alone can answer "did any resolve happen":

- `test_the_manifest_owns_the_provider_inert_answer`
- `test_a_pause_apply_does_not_sweep_every_provider` — zero `resolve_provider` calls, no refresh task, under one provider's cost
- `test_a_no_op_pause_costs_no_provider_work_either`
- `test_a_provider_key_change_still_rebuilds_and_sweeps` — the negative case
- `test_a_cancelled_sweep_does_not_block_the_next_replace` — the yield, asserted by cancelling one scheduling turn in

`tests/api/test_admin_route_pause.py::test_the_next_plan_after_a_pause_apply_honours_it` — through the real endpoint and the real apply path: the ref keeps its place in the chain and is absent from `usable_indexes`.

`tests/providers/test_failure_policy.py::test_the_bare_word_billing_is_not_a_quota_phrase` — a 400 saying *"see our billing documentation for limits"* stays `invalid_request`. The `generic_billing` row of `test_every_measured_billing_phrase_classifies_as_quota`, which existed only to exercise the bare word, is removed with it.

jsdom, in `test_admin_static_jsdom.py` + `admin_jsdom_harness.mjs` (fault injection for a refusal body, a transport failure, and a held-open response):

- `test_a_failed_pause_announces_a_failure_in_the_route_status_panel`
- `test_a_failed_pause_leaves_the_row_in_its_previous_state`
- `test_undo_disables_the_row_control_while_it_is_in_flight`

jsdom alone, `-n 0`: **199 passed** (196 before).

## Residual risks

1. **The provider-inert set is exactly the six pause keys.** `MODEL`, `MODEL_*_FALLBACKS` and the visibility keys still trigger a full rebuild and sweep, deliberately: they can name a provider whose catalogue is not cached, and being wrong there is worse than being slow. If the user wants route edits fast too, that is a separate, better-evidenced change.
2. **`await asyncio.sleep(0)` changes cancellation timing for every config apply**, not just pause. It is the correct change and it has its own test, but it touches a shared path.
3. **The event-loop stall is now prevented, not measured.** I did not drive `/v1/messages` concurrently with a pause before and after; the mechanism is confirmed from the code and the yield removes it, but the stall itself was never timed.
4. **The scratch numbers are this machine's.** The scratch env carries a fake key for all 52 credential-bearing providers, so its sweep is broader than the user's live 17-19 and the before-figures are correspondingly larger than the ~2 s in the original investigation. The after-figure — zero provider work per click — is the transferable one.
5. **Nothing was verified against the live 8082 server**, which was read-only throughout and never restarted. The measurements are the scratch server's.

## CI note

Local full-suite baseline on this machine is **15** known failures unrelated to this branch (env leaks from the real `~/.fcc` and PowerShell installer/jsdom flake under full parallel load); the suite was re-run with a redirected `HOME` before believing anything in `tests/websearch` or `test_provider_manager`.

fix(admin): a pause writes the pause, and nothing else

Every admin write asked ProviderRuntimeManager.replace for its default
background sweep, so a pause click rebuilt every provider client and
re-queried every provider's /models before it answered. A pause is read off
Settings at plan time and never reaches create_provider, so none of that work
can change what a pause does. Measured on a scratch server with the user's
route shape and fake keys: 6934-13156 ms per click and 52
"ProviderRateLimiter initialized" lines per click, before; 638-772 ms and
zero, after. The residual is prepare_admin_update validation at 628-643 ms,
which is a separate change to the whole admin write path.

background_refresh is now computed from the update at the call site, and the
decision is a manifest fact rather than a key list written at the caller:
ConfigFieldSpec carries affects_providers, defaulting True so a key added
later is slow-but-correct rather than fast-but-wrong, and the six
MODEL_*_PAUSED fields declare False beside their own help text. The
generation swap is kept -- it costs under a millisecond and it is what makes
a pause visible to the very next plan.

The discovery resolve loop now yields per provider. It built an SSL context
and an HTTP client for each one with no await in the loop, so the task
reached no suspension point until the whole sweep had run: the event loop was
held for its full length, and _cancel_refresh's cancel could not land until
the sweep it was abandoning had finished, which is why one click paid for the
one before it.

Two UI defects go with it. A failed pause reported only into #messageArea at
the top of the page, so the pause control's own panel said nothing and the
row snapped back with no explanation; it now announces the failure in
#routeStatus, without an Undo button, and keeps the message area too. Undo
passed button: null, leaving the row's own toggle live during its POST; it
passes the originating button, so one guard covers both writes. Pause
semantics are unchanged: it stays per rail, and USAGE and the in-app Guide
now say that plainly instead of the button meaning something new.

Separately, QUOTA_PHRASES no longer contains the bare word billing. The
condition on that classifier was no false positives and one bare word cannot
meet it: it matches "see our billing documentation for limits" in an ordinary
400, which would bench a whole key pool for a merely malformed request. It is
not replaced by a narrower phrase, because no measured provider body was on
hand to justify one.
